title: Multiple Hypothesis Testing in Pattern Discovery
sections_checked: Section 4 family-wise error theory and minP condition
evidence_note: Provides a generic multiple-hypothesis procedure for pattern mining that strongly controls FWER under its stated minP condition, with evaluation on real and generated data. It predates the sampled 2010 substring paper, so broad multiplicity correction is not a novel opportunity. It does not directly evaluate overlapping contiguous substring scans or their data-derived probability baseline.

title: Mining Statistically Significant Substrings using the Chi-Square Statistic
sections_checked: Introduction: p-value and chi-square significance under a memoryless multinomial model
Section 8 conclusions and explicitly open asymptotic/correlation questions
evidence_note: A later, direct substring-mining paper defines per-substring p-values under a memoryless Bernoulli/multinomial model and proposes a faster algorithm; its conclusion says rigorous proof of the maximum-statistic asymptotics and extension to correlated/Markov strings remain open. This narrows the 2010 study's scope but neither replicates nor refutes its ARLM/AGMM scores or establishes their multiple-scan error rate.

title: HoloClean: Holistic Data Repairs with Probabilistic Inference
sections_checked: Section 6.1 four real datasets, ground-truth protocol and baselines
evidence_note: The later HoloClean paper evaluates four real datasets (1,000 to 2,071,849 tuples), reports average repair precision about 90%, recall about 76%, and >2x average F1 gain versus its compared systems. This is counterevidence to any broad claim that data cleaning lacks cross-domain real-data studies, but HoloClean combines constraints, external information and statistical signals and is not a direct replication of the 2012 Bayesian approach. For Food and Physicians, the authors manually label 2,000/2,500 cells and caution recall estimates may be biased.

title: Faster approximate subgraph counts with privacy
sections_checked: Related work on recursive mechanism and privacy-model scope
evidence_note: This later work studies faster approximate-sensitivity algorithms for edge-private graph counting and cites recursive mechanisms among prior methods. It explicitly states its fast triangle-counting technique is edge-DP-specific and new ideas are needed to extend it to node-DP. It is contextual evidence that privacy-unit differences remain important, not a direct evaluation or contradiction of the 2013 node-DP theorem or its node-private motif accuracy results.
